import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    x = feats.x
    y = feats.y
    
    # Calculate correlations and identify near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(x.T)
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(ids[j])
    
    # Remove near-duplicates
    keep_indices = [i for i in range(len(ids)) if ids[i] not in to_remove]
    keep_ids = [ids[i] for i in keep_indices]
    
    # Compute effect sizes (mean difference in outcome groups)
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(keep_ids):
        group0 = x[y==0, i]
        group1 = x[y==1, i]
        mean_diff = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
        effect_sizes.append(abs(mean_diff))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    sorted_idx = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    sorted_ids = [keep_ids[i] for i in sorted_idx]
    
    # Select top drivers (max MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = tuple(sorted_ids[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, len(sorted_ids))])
    
    # For columns, use all features with significant effect (p < 0.1)
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Simple logistic regression approach: select features with large effect sizes
    for i, fid in enumerate(keep_ids):
        group0 = x[y==0, i]
        group1 = x[y==1, i]
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1)
        if p_val < 0.1 or abs(np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)) > 0.1:
            columns.append(fid)
            
            # Add interaction terms for top features
            if len(columns) <= 3 and len(columns) > 1:
                # Add pairwise products between top features
                for prev_fid in columns[:-1]:
                    products.append((prev_fid, fid))
    
    # Create weighted loading for top features
    for i, fid in enumerate(columns[:3]):
        loadings[fid] = effect_sizes[keep_ids.index(fid)]
    
    return Design(
        drivers=drivers,
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
